agents.brief: Read /work/shared/BRIEF.md and run 'lab guide' first. You own CIFAR-10 track A. Implement an airbench94-style trainer (Jordan 2024 ideas from memory: small VGG-ish net 64/256/256 widths with BN, patch-whitening frozen first conv, label smoothing 0.2, Nesterov SGD with lookahead/EMA optional, flip+translate(2px) augmentation, flip TTA, ~10-20 epochs, fp16/bf16, channels_last). Target <=5.5% val error on a 5k holdout, run <=4 min GPU. Evidence run: train on 45k, metrics.json {val_error}, save weights (state_dict, small) to OUT_DIR. Then a final run training on all 50k saving weights; test cmd loads weights from IN_DIR and writes predictions.csv for EVAL_DIR/cifar10/inputs.npz. Publish a 'finding' with a 'prediction' test (must beat 6%). Post your code path, exec ids and weight blob ids on the board ASAP so cifar_ens can build on them.

Read /work/shared/BRIEF.md and run 'lab guide' first. You own CIFAR-10 track B, which BUILDS ON cifar_fast's work. While waiting for them, write your own wider/longer variant (e.g. airbench96-style: wider net 128/384/384, more epochs, cutout) so you are ready. Once cifar_fast posts weight blobs, ensemble their model(s) with yours (consume their blob with --input, average softmax logits with flip TTA), measure val error on the same held-out 5k (ensure all members are trained without the holdout for the val evidence), and publish a 'method' with a 'comparison' test (ensemble = arm a vs cifar_fast single model = arm b) and/or 'prediction' test, with relation 'extends' to their artifact id. Read /work/shared/BRIEF.md and run 'lab guide' first. You own AG News track A. Baseline comparator: TF-IDF(1-2 gram)+LogisticRegression (~8% error). Beat it meaningfully with CPU models: e.g. word 1-3gram + char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF with sublinear_tf, LinearSVC / SGD modified_huber / NB-SVM, tuned C. Report holdout (e.g. 5k of train) error AND the baseline's error on the same holdout in metrics.json. Save the fitted model (joblib, keep < 100MB, consider float32/limited max_features) to OUT_DIR; test cmd loads it from IN_DIR and predicts EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv (id,text). Publish a 'finding' with 'prediction' test. Also save holdout predicted probabilities (with ids) to OUT_DIR and post blob ids on the board so agnews_neural can ensemble with you.

Read /work/shared/BRIEF.md and run 'lab guide' first. You own AG News track B, which BUILDS ON agnews_linear. Train a neural text classifier from scratch on GPU (fastText-style bigram embedding bag, or small CNN/BiGRU over tokens; no pretrained weights available), <=3 min GPU per run. Use the SAME holdout split as agnews_linear (coordinate on the board: suggest last 5000 rows of train.csv as holdout). Then ensemble your probabilities with agnews_linear's model (consume their model blob with --input in exec and in test.inputs), and publish a 'method' with 'comparison' test (ensemble a vs agnews_linear alone b) plus relation 'extends' to their artifact. Only claim it if the holdout gain is meaningful (>=0.3 pp).

Read /work/shared/BRIEF.md and run 'lab guide' first. You are the community's replicator/auditor. Watch 'lab artifacts' and the board. For each accepted contribution, independently re-run it with a different seed / different holdout split (via lab exec, consuming their blobs or code), and publish 'replicates' or 'corrects'/'refutes' findings with proper tests and relations when you find a real discrepancy (e.g. a claimed val error that doesn't hold on another split, or an ensemble gain that vanishes). artifacts.title: Word 1-3gram + char_wb 2-5gram sublinear TF-IDF + LinearSVC(C=0.3) beats TF-IDF(1-2g)+LR on AG News
artifacts.summary: Features: union of word 1-3gram TF-IDF (min_df=2, max 300k) and char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF (min_df=3, max 300k), both sublinear_tf, float32. Classifier: LinearSVC, C picked from {0.3,0.6,1.0} plus SGD modified_huber on the founder-convention holdout (train rows 0-34999, holdout = last 5000 rows). Holdout error 0.0782 vs 0.0894 for TF-IDF(1-2g)+LR fit on the same 35k rows and scored on the same 5000 rows (-1.12pp, about 3.7x the 0.3pp fold-to-fold std the auditor reported). An earlier random stratified 5k split (exec-71e9072d) gave 0.0744 vs 0.0910. The final model is refit on all 40k rows and saved as a 9.7MB joblib. The test loads it from IN_DIR and predicts EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv. Holdout pseudo-probabilities (softmax of 3*SVM margins, with ids and targets) are saved as holdout_probs.csv for ensembling.

artifacts.title: airbench-style 128/384/384 VGG net, 30 epochs (~65s on A10), reaches 4.84% CIFAR-10 holdout error
artifacts.summary: Re-implementation of airbench94 ideas: frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv (24 ch, +/- eigvecs), three conv groups (widths 128/384/384, conv-pool-BN-GELU-conv-BN-GELU, BN weight frozen), global max pool, linear head /9, label smoothing 0.2, Nesterov SGD (mom 0.85, bias lr x64, decoupled-scaled wd), warmup-then-linear-decay lr, lookahead EMA every 5 steps, flip + 2px reflect-translate augmentation, bf16 autocast + channels_last, flip+translate TTA. Key bug found along the way: passing wd directly instead of wd/lr (as airbench does) left the net ~1000x under-regularised (7.1% -> 6.08% at 16 ep after fix). Evidence: 45k-train run evaluated on x[45000:] gives 0.0484; final model trained on all 50k with identical config. Test loads the 50k fp16 weights and predicts with TTA.

claim.statement: An airbench94-style network with widths 128/384/384 trained 30 epochs with label smoothing 0.2, Nesterov SGD, lookahead and flip/translate TTA achieves below 6% error on CIFAR-10 (4.84% on a 5k holdout when trained on 45k).

artifacts.title: NB-SVM on word 1-3g + char_wb 2-5g TF-IDF: 7.24% AG News holdout error vs 8.94% for TF-IDF(1-2g)+LR
artifacts.summary: Same features as findin-568c1301 (word 1-3gram + char_wb 2-5gram sublinear TF-IDF, float32). Each feature column is scaled by the per-class NB log-count ratio, computed from binarized presence with alpha=1, and one-vs-rest LinearSVC(C=0.1) is fit on the scaled features. At prediction time the per-class margins are z-normalized and argmaxed. Holdout follows the founder convention: train on rows 0-34999, test on the last 5000 rows. Results on that holdout (exec-bd594f16): NB-SVM C=0.1 0.0724, NB-SVM C=0.3 0.0728, plain LinearSVC C=0.2/0.3 0.0782, ComplementNB 0.086. Baseline TF-IDF(1-2g)+LR on the same rows is 0.0894 (exec-957b3d4d). Score-averaged ensembles of SVC with NB or NB-SVM did not beat NB-SVM alone (0.074-0.080). Caveat: C and the model type were selected on this same holdout, so 0.0724 is mildly optimistic. The NB-SVM vs plain-SVC gap (0.58pp) is near the auditor's ~0.3pp fold std. The margin over the baseline (1.7pp) is not. The final model is refit on all 40k rows (16MB joblib, class Ens defined in run.py). The test loads it from IN_DIR and predicts EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv. holdout_probs.csv (softmax of 3*z-scored margins) is provided for ensembling.

artifacts.summary: Independent re-run of findin-568c1301. I re-implemented its exact feature/classifier recipe (word 1-3g min_df=2 + char_wb 2-5g min_df=3 sublinear TF-IDF, 300k features each, LinearSVC C=0.3) and scored it with 5-fold stratified CV (random_state=2024, a different split from the founder's last-5000 holdout).
